tests.title: A sync against an unchanged origin reports up to date
given: a ready standard workspace whose origin is at the same commit as its branch
tests.when: the sync route is called
then: the response is 200 with the workspace
last_sync_at is the time of this sync
head_sha is unchanged and sync_error is null
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file: r = post(sync); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.head_sha == before and r.json.sync_error is None

tests.title: A sync fast-forwards the branch when origin has advanced
given: a ready standard workspace whose origin has two commits the workspace lacks
tests.when: the sync route is called
then: the response is 200
head_sha and upstream_head_sha both equal origin's head
last_sync_at is updated and sync_error is null
the branch in the repository is at origin's head
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file: assert post(sync).json.head_sha == origin_head and store_ref(branch) == origin_head

tests.title: reset_to_upstream moves the branch whatever the ancestry
given: a ready standard workspace whose origin was force-pushed to an unrelated commit
tests.when: the sync route is called with reset_to_upstream true
then: the response is 200
head_sha and upstream_head_sha equal origin's head
sync_error is null
the branch moved although origin's head does not descend from the previous local head
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file: r = post(sync + '?reset_to_upstream=true'); assert r.json.head_sha == origin_head

tests.title: A diverged origin is refused with a recovery instruction
given: a ready standard workspace whose origin was force-pushed
tests.when: the sync route is called without reset_to_upstream
then: the response is 409
sync_error is set and names reset_to_upstream
head_sha is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file: assert post(sync).status == 409 and 'reset_to_upstream' in read().json.sync_error

tests.title: A failed fetch answers 502 and records the error without a credential
given: a workspace whose origin is unreachable, one whose origin refuses the credential, and one whose credential cannot be resolved
tests.when: the sync route is called for each
then: each answers 502
sync_error is set in each case and contains no credential
head_sha and upstream_head_sha are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file, table over the three failures asserting 502, a set sync_error and the absence of the token

tests.title: A cancelled sync answers 504 and leaves a recoverable workspace
given: a sync whose fetch is made to exceed its deadline, and one whose client disconnects
tests.when: each is run
then: each answers 504
sync_error is set
a later sync of the same workspace succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file: assert post(sync).status == 504; assert post(sync).status == 200 once the fetch is healthy

tests.title: A successful sync clears an earlier error
given: a workspace whose last sync failed and left sync_error set
tests.when: a sync succeeds
then: sync_error is null afterwards
the field reflects the present condition rather than the history
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file: assert read().json.sync_error is not None; fix_origin(); assert post(sync).json.sync_error is None

tests.title: A sync is refused for a workspace that is not ready or has syncing disabled
given: workspaces at pending, cloning, failed and archived, and a ready one with sync_enabled false
tests.when: the sync route is called for each
then: each answers 400
no fetch is attempted
no workspace field changes
tests.pseudocode: in the sync test file, table over the five cases asserting 400 and remote.fetches == 0

tests.title: A sync against a busy workspace is refused at once
given: a ready workspace whose lock is held by a long operation
tests.when: the sync route is called, and again after the lock is released
then: the first answers 409 with error_type workspace_busy
it answers without waiting for the lock
the second succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the sync test file: assert post(sync).json.error.error_type == 'workspace_busy'; release(); assert post(sync).status == 200

tests.title: A sync in progress is not a stored status
given: a ready workspace and a sync made to run slowly
tests.when: the workspace is read while the sync runs, and a second sync is attempted
then: the workspace's status reads ready throughout
the second sync is refused with workspace_busy and not by a status check
tests.pseudocode: in the sync integration test file: start_slow_sync(); assert read().json.status == 'ready' and post(sync).json.error.error_type == 'workspace_busy'

tests.title: A reclone pushes out, discards and copies again
given: a ready workspace with a usable credential, a branch that exists only in its repository, and sync_error and upstream_head_sha set
tests.when: the reclone route is called and the workspace is polled to a terminal status
then: the response is 200 with status pending, sync_error null and upstream_head_sha null
the local-only branch exists on origin afterwards
the workspace reaches ready with a freshly copied repository
tests.pseudocode: in the reclone integration test file: r = post(reclone); assert r.json.status == 'pending' and localOnly in remote_refs(); assert poll() == 'ready'

tests.title: A reclone proceeds although its push failed
given: a workspace whose origin refuses the push, and one with no usable credential
tests.when: the reclone route is called for each
then: each answers 200 with status pending
each repository is copied again
the push failure does not appear as the route's answer
tests.pseudocode: in the reclone integration test file, table over the two cases asserting 200 and a completed re-copy

tests.title: A reclone is refused for an archived, copying or busy workspace
given: an archived workspace, one at pending, one at cloning, and a ready one whose lock is held
tests.when: the reclone route is called for each
then: the archived one answers 400
the copying ones answer 409
the busy one answers 409 with error_type workspace_busy
no repository is discarded
tests.pseudocode: in the reclone test file, table over the four cases asserting the status and that the repository still exists

tests.title: A reclone that cannot discard the repository fails without changing the workspace
given: a store whose discard raises, and a store whose workspace update raises
tests.when: the reclone route is called against each
then: each answers 500
the workspace keeps its previous status
the repository still exists
tests.pseudocode: in the reclone test file: with discard raising, assert post(reclone).status == 500 and read().json.status == before

tests.title: The branch push checks run in the documented order
given: combinations where two checks would both fail: a PAT without the scope for a slug naming nothing, a member pushing to an unready workspace, an invalid branch name on an unready workspace, a patch branch on a busy workspace, and a missing branch without force
tests.when: each combination is requested
then: each answers the refusal belonging to the earlier check
a PAT without the scope answers 403 even for a slug that names nothing
the patch-branch refusal is given although the workspace is busy
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, table over (conditions, expectedStatus, expectedErrorType)

tests.title: The branch name is one segment decoded exactly once
given: branches named fix/42-nil-map, a%25b and plain
tests.when: the route is called with fix%2F42-nil-map, a%2525b, plain, and with an unescaped slash in the path
then: each escaped form names the intended branch
a%2525b names a%25b and not a%b
the unescaped slash matches no route and answers 404
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, table over (segment, expectedBranchName)

tests.title: An invalid branch name is refused with the rule it broke
given: names starting with a hyphen, containing two dots, containing a control character, ending with .lock, and an empty name
tests.when: the route is called for each
then: each answers 404 with error_type branch_not_found
each message begins "branch_not_found: " and names the rule broken
nothing is pushed
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, table over the invalid names asserting the status, type and message prefix

tests.title: An unready workspace or a malformed body is refused, and a thin body is accepted
given: workspaces at pending, cloning, failed and archived, and a ready one
tests.when: the route is called on each, and on the ready one with no body, {}, a body with unknown fields, a non-object body and a non-boolean force
then: each unready workspace answers 400
the non-object body and the non-boolean force answer 400
no body, {} and unknown fields are accepted and push without force
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, two tables over the workspace statuses and the body shapes

tests.title: The branches this route will not push are refused by kind
given: a carry_patch workspace with an integration branch and a registered patch that is not deleted, and a workspace with its own branch set
tests.when: each of those branches is pushed, with the workspace's lock free and again with it held, and the workspace's own branch is pushed with force
then: the integration branch answers 400 integration_branch
the registered patch answers 400 patch_branch
the workspace's own branch with force answers 400 protected_branch
each answer is the same whether or not the lock is held
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, table over (branchKind, lockHeld, expectedErrorType)

tests.title: A branch push against a busy workspace is refused at once
given: a ready workspace whose lock is held, and an ordinary branch
tests.when: the route is called, and again after the lock is released
then: the first answers 409 with error_type workspace_busy without waiting
the second succeeds
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file: assert post(push).json.error.error_type == 'workspace_busy'

tests.title: Forced pushes are protected against HEAD and missing branches
given: a workspace with no branch set whose HEAD points at main, and a name the repository lacks
tests.when: main is pushed with force, and the missing branch is pushed with and without force
then: main with force answers 400 protected_branch
the missing branch answers 404 branch_not_found with the message naming it
nothing is pushed in either case
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, table over the three cases asserting status, error_type and remote.pushes == 0

tests.title: A successful push answers with the documented body
given: a ready workspace with a branch origin does not have
tests.when: the branch is pushed
then: the response is 200 with branch, sha, remote and remote_url
sha is the 40-character tip that was offered to origin
remote is "origin"
the branch is on origin at that commit
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push integration test file: r = post(push); assert r.json.remote == 'origin' and len(r.json.sha) == 40 and remote_ref(branch) == r.json.sha

tests.title: The result distinguishes pushed, up_to_date and forced
given: a branch origin lacks, a branch origin already has at the same commit, and a branch origin has at a divergent commit
tests.when: each is pushed, the unchanged one twice and the divergent one with force, and the unchanged one once more with force
then: the new branch reports pushed
the unchanged branch reports up_to_date, with and without force
the divergent branch with force reports forced
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push integration test file, table over (originState, force, expectedResult)

tests.title: remote_url is reported without userinfo
given: workspaces whose git_url is https with userinfo, https without, and an scp-style address
tests.when: a branch is pushed in each
then: the https URL with userinfo is reported without it
the plain https URL is unchanged
the scp-style address is reported exactly as stored
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, table over (gitUrl, expectedRemoteUrl)

tests.title: A push finishes although its caller went away
given: a ready workspace and a push whose transfer takes measurable time
tests.when: the client disconnects after the request is sent and before the answer
then: the branch reaches origin at the offered commit
the outcome is recorded as if the caller had waited
calling the route again reports up_to_date
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push integration test file: send_and_disconnect(); assert eventually(remote_ref(branch) == tip); assert post(push).json.result == 'up_to_date'

tests.title: A non-fast-forward push is refused with the right instruction
given: origin ahead of the workspace on an ordinary branch, the same on the workspace's own branch, an origin whose refs cannot be listed, and an origin that refuses even a forced update
tests.when: each is pushed
then: each answers 409 with error_type non_fast_forward
the ordinary branch's message names origin's commit and ends with the instruction to push with force
the workspace's own branch's message ends with the instruction to sync
the forced refusal says origin refuses non-fast-forward updates even with force
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push integration test file, table over the four cases asserting the status, type and message ending

tests.title: A missing repository and a refused ref map to their own answers
given: an origin that answers not found, and one that refuses the ref with a reason
tests.when: a branch is pushed against each
then: the first answers 404 with error_type forge_not_found
the second answers 422 with error_type forge_rejected carrying origin's reason
the reason is scrubbed of any credential
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push integration test file, table over the two origins asserting status, type and a scrubbed message

tests.title: Authentication, connection and deadline failures map to their own answers
given: origins answering 401 and 403, one unreachable, one answering unreadably, one exceeding the two-minute deadline, and a workspace with no stored credential
tests.when: a branch is pushed against each
then: 401 and 403 answer 502 with forge_unauthenticated and forge_forbidden
the unreachable and unreadable origins answer 502 with forge_unreachable and forge_error
the deadline answers 504 with forge_timeout
the forge_unauthenticated message says whether no credential was stored or which kind origin rejected
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push integration test file, table over the six cases asserting status and error_type

tests.title: This route's own error types are repeated at the start of the message
given: one failure for each of this route's own error types
tests.when: each answer is produced
then: each message begins with its error_type followed by a colon and a space
an answer shared with other routes, such as workspace_busy, keeps its usual message
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, table over the route's error types asserting message.startswith(f'{type}: ')

tests.title: No answer of either route leaks a credential, userinfo or a git error
given: a workspace whose credential and whose git_url userinfo are distinctive, and a git transport whose error text is distinctive
tests.when: every failure answer of the sync, reclone and branch push routes is produced
then: no response body contains the credential
none contains the userinfo
none contains the transport's own error text
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push test file, over every failure case: assert CRED not in body and USERINFO not in body and GITERR not in body

tests.title: A sync fast-forwards a workspace against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, a ready standard workspace and a real remote that has advanced
tests.when: afc workspace sync is run
then: the command exits 0 and prints the workspace
head_sha and upstream_head_sha are at the remote's head
last_sync_at is set and sync_error is null
tests.pseudocode: in the sync smoke test file: r = run('afc workspace sync', slug); assert r.exit == 0 and json(r.stdout).head_sha == remote_head

tests.title: A rewritten remote is refused and then recovered with reset_to_upstream
given: a running deployment and a workspace whose real remote was force-pushed
tests.when: afc workspace sync is run, then run again with --reset-to-upstream
then: the first exits 1 and the workspace's sync_error names reset_to_upstream
the second exits 0 and the branch is at the remote's head
sync_error is cleared
tests.pseudocode: in the sync smoke test file: assert run('afc workspace sync').exit == 1; assert run('afc workspace sync --reset-to-upstream').exit == 0

tests.title: A branch pushed to Parley reaches the forge
given: a running deployment, a workspace, and a branch with a slash in its name pushed to Parley's git server
tests.when: afc workspace push is run for that branch
then: the command exits 0 and prints result pushed with the branch and the SHA
the branch exists on the real remote at that commit
remote_url carries no credentials
tests.pseudocode: in the branch push smoke test file: run('git push', hub_url, 'fix/42'); r = run('afc workspace push', slug, 'fix/42'); assert json(r.stdout).result == 'pushed'

tests.title: A reclone recovers a workspace against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a workspace whose repository has been made unusable
tests.when: afc workspace reclone --confirm is run and the workspace is polled
then: the command exits 0 and prints status pending
the workspace reaches ready
branches that existed only in the old repository are on the remote
tests.pseudocode: in the reclone smoke test file: r = run('afc workspace reclone --confirm', slug); assert json(r.stdout).status == 'pending'; assert poll() == 'ready'
